title: Magnitude 7.7 Earthquake Strikes Indonesia, Triggering Tsunami Warning
excerpt: A powerful undersea earthquake near Flores Island was followed by three aftershocks, with the USGS estimating 500,000 people exposed to severe shaking. Indonesia's geophysics agency issued a tsunami warning for coastal regions.
body:
• A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off Indonesia's Flores Island at 4:58 a.m. local time Saturday (9:58 p.m. GMT Friday) at a depth of 35 km, followed by three aftershocks of magnitudes 5.9, 5.6, and 6.1
  • Indonesia's BMKG geophysics agency issued a tsunami warning for coastal regions, urging residents to move to higher ground and stay away from beaches and riverbanks
  • The USGS estimates approximately 500,000 people were exposed to very strong or severe shaking, with potential for moderate damage to well-built structures and significant damage to poorly built ones
  • Australia's tsunami warning centre said there is no tsunami threat to the Australian mainland, islands, or territories

A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia near Flores Island early Saturday morning local time, triggering a tsunami warning and at least three significant aftershocks as the country's disaster response agencies scrambled to assess the situation.

The European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre recorded the main quake at approximately 4:58 a.m. local time (2158 GMT Friday) at a depth of 35 kilometers (21.75 miles), according to Reuters. The US Geological Survey confirmed the magnitude and reported aftershocks of 5.9, 5.6, and 6.1 in quick succession.

Tsunami Warning Issued

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) immediately issued an early tsunami warning for several coastal regions. The agency urged residents along impacted coastlines to move to higher ground and stay away from beaches and riverbanks, according to the Associated Press.

The warning reflects the potential danger from shallow undersea earthquakes in the region. BMKG identified the quake as occurring near Flores Island, part of Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara province. Australia's tsunami warning centre separately confirmed that the earthquake poses no tsunami threat to the Australian mainland, islands, or territories.

Scale of Exposure

Initial USGS estimates paint a concerning picture of the quake's reach. The agency's PAGER system suggests approximately 500,000 people were exposed to very strong or severe shaking — intensity levels capable of causing slight to moderate damage in well-built structures and significant damage in poorly built ones.

The Indonesian government had not yet released official casualty or damage reports as of Saturday morning, though the USGS assessment indicates both are possible based on shaking intensity and regional building standards.

Ring of Fire Vulnerability

Indonesia sits squarely on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific Ocean where tectonic plates meet, producing frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity. The ring is one of the most seismically active zones on Earth, stretching from Japan and Indonesia on one side of the Pacific to California and South America on the other.

"Although relatively small, this situation still requires vigilance due to the potential for aftershocks."

— Indonesia's National Disaster Agency

The country's earthquake history underscores the stakes. The catastrophic 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, triggered by a magnitude 9.1 quake off Sumatra, killed more than 220,000 people across the region — more than half in Indonesia. In 2018, a magnitude 6.9 earthquake killed hundreds on the island of Lombok, and a separate 7.5 magnitude quake and tsunami struck Sulawesi later that year. Most recently, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake in the Northern Molucca Sea in April 2026 killed one person and triggered tsunami waves up to 0.75 meters.

Indian Diaspora in the Region

Indonesia is home to a small but established Indian community, primarily concentrated in Jakarta and Bali. Indian nationals working in trade, technology, and tourism sectors, along with travelers visiting the popular tourist destination, may be affected by the quake's impact on infrastructure and transportation.

Developing Situation

This remains a developing story. Authorities are continuing to monitor aftershock activity and assess potential damage. Residents in coastal areas under the tsunami warning have been advised to remain on higher ground until authorities issue an all-clear. International disaster response agencies are standing by to assist if requested.
